ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-instance view information gain estimated with a conditional entropy bound
PROPOSAL: We quantify, for each training image, how much a given augmented view adds beyond what the model already encodes, using a conditional entropy estimate computed from the embedding of the anchor and of the view under a small variational decoder trained alongside a SimCLR encoder. We train a ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100 with the standard augmentation set, log the per-instance gain for each augmentation family across training, and relate it to the final linear probe accuracy of the classes those instances belong to. The output is a map from augmentation family and training stage to estimated information contributed, which we then use to reweight augmentation sampling in a second run.
CONTROLS: The same encoder with uniform augmentation sampling, reweighting by a random per-instance score with the same distribution, reweighting by the InfoNCE loss of the pair instead of the entropy estimate, and a frozen-encoder variant of the estimator to check that the gain signal is not an artefact of co-training, three seeds each.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: Gains should be largest early in training and for colour-based augmentations, and reweighting should improve linear probe accuracy on CIFAR-100 by around one point at batch 256. If reweighting by a random score matches it, the estimator carries no instance-specific signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Feature-space view expansion gated by neighbourhood agreement at small batch
PROPOSAL: We generate additional positive views for each instance directly in the embedding space of a MoCo v2 encoder by moving the anchor embedding along directions sampled from the covariance of its nearest neighbours in the queue, and we admit a synthetic view only when its nearest-neighbour label agreement with the anchor, measured on a frozen copy of the encoder, stays above a threshold set on a validation split. Training runs on STL-10 and ImageNet-100 with a ResNet-50 at batch sizes of 64 and 256, and we evaluate linear probe and kNN accuracy as well as alignment and uniformity on the test set.
CONTROLS: The comparison includes the same encoder trained with image-space augmentations only at both batch sizes, the same encoder at batch 1024 as an upper reference point, synthetic views drawn along random isotropic directions of the same norm, and synthetic views admitted without the agreement gate, so that the contribution of the gate can be separated from that of the expansion itself.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: Gated expansion should close most of the gap between batch 64 and batch 1024 on ImageNet-100 kNN accuracy, while ungated expansion should degrade alignment. If random directions perform as well as covariance directions, the neighbourhood structure is not what helps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Augmentation policy optimised against an information criterion rather than downstream accuracy
PROPOSAL: We learn an augmentation policy for SimCLR whose objective is a per-instance information criterion: the policy, a small network over augmentation magnitudes, is updated to maximise a variational lower bound on the mutual information between views while a semantic penalty, the disagreement between the two views under a frozen supervised classifier trained on a disjoint labelled split, is kept below a fixed level. We train a ResNet-50 on ImageNet-100 and a ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, modelling magnitudes for cropping, colour jitter, blur and solarisation, and we evaluate linear probe accuracy and transfer to Oxford Pets and Flowers.
CONTROLS: Fixed SimCLR augmentations, a policy optimised directly for a proxy downstream accuracy as in learned-augmentation work, a policy trained without the semantic penalty, and a randomised policy with the same marginal distribution of magnitudes, each with three seeds.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: The information-optimised policy should match the accuracy-optimised one on in-domain linear probing and generalise better on transfer. Removing the semantic penalty should push magnitudes upward and lower accuracy, showing where the trade-off lies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing mutual information estimators as predictors of what each view contributes
PROPOSAL: We ask whether the mutual information (MI) between two views of the same instance, estimated per instance, predicts how useful that instance's augmentations are for representation quality. We train a residual network (ResNet) with 18 layers using the simple framework for contrastive learning of visual representations (SimCLR) on the CIFAR-100 dataset from the Canadian Institute for Advanced Research and on a 100-class subset of ImageNet, and we obtain three per-instance MI estimates during training: the information noise-contrastive estimation (InfoNCE) bound, a nearest-neighbour entropy estimate in embedding space, and a variational bound with a learned critic. We then remove augmentations for the instances in the top and bottom deciles of each estimate and measure the change in linear probe and k-nearest-neighbour (kNN) accuracy.
CONTROLS: Removal of augmentations for random deciles of the same size, removal guided by loss value rather than MI, and the three estimators evaluated on a frozen encoder at the end of training, with three seeds per setting.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Instances in the bottom decile of estimated MI should be the ones whose augmentation removal hurts least, with the variational bound ranking instances most consistently across seeds. If random deciles produce the same change, per-instance MI carries no actionable information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Small-batch contrastive learning with per-instance adaptive temperature driven by view agreement
PROPOSAL: We test whether the trade-off between invariance and expressivity can be managed per instance by setting the InfoNCE temperature of each anchor from the agreement between its views: anchors whose views already agree closely receive a lower temperature that sharpens separation from neighbours, while anchors whose views disagree receive a higher temperature that tolerates the spread. Agreement is the cosine similarity between view embeddings under a momentum encoder. We train ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 encoders on CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet-100 at batch sizes 32, 128 and 512 and measure linear probe accuracy, kNN accuracy, alignment and uniformity.
CONTROLS: A fixed temperature tuned per batch size, a global temperature schedule that decays over training, a temperature assigned from a shuffled agreement vector, and the same adaptive rule applied to a MoCo variant with a queue so that the effect is not specific to in-batch negatives, each over three seeds.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: Adaptive temperature should help most at batch 32, narrowing the gap to batch 512 by roughly a third on ImageNet-100, and should give nothing at batch 512. If the shuffled assignment performs the same, the gain comes from the temperature distribution rather than from instance-level matching.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A controlled synthetic benchmark for separating semantic invariance from view expressivity
PROPOSAL: We construct an image dataset from a rendering pipeline in which each instance has known semantic factors (object identity and shape) and known nuisance factors (pose, lighting, background and texture), so that for any augmentation the information shared between views and the information lost about each factor can be computed exactly from the generative model. On this dataset we train SimCLR and BYOL encoders with augmentations that vary which nuisance factors they randomise and how strongly, and we measure, for each factor, the conditional entropy of that factor given the representation, together with linear probe accuracy on identity and on pose.
CONTROLS: Supervised training on identity as the invariance limit, an autoencoder as the expressivity limit, augmentations that randomise the semantic factors themselves to confirm that identity accuracy collapses, and a transfer check on real images from a matching object category benchmark.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Linear probe accuracy on identity should rise and pose accuracy fall monotonically as the augmentation randomises more nuisance factors, with the crossing point predicted by the computed information quantities. The prediction fails if the exact quantities and the measured probe accuracies disagree on which augmentation setting is best, which would indicate that optimisation effects dominate the information picture.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Replacing large batches with an instance-conditioned negative bank for hardware-constrained contrastive training
PROPOSAL: We ask whether the diversity usually obtained from large batches can be recovered by maintaining, for each instance, a small set of hard negatives selected by a momentum encoder from a queue and refreshed every epoch, so that each anchor sees a few informative negatives instead of thousands of random ones. We implement this on top of MoCo v2 with a ResNet-50 on ImageNet-100 and a ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100, with effective batch sizes of 32 and 64, and we compare representation quality by linear probe accuracy, kNN accuracy and the uniformity statistic, together with a measure of false negative rate using labels only at evaluation time.
CONTROLS: MoCo v2 with the standard queue at the same small batches, SimCLR at batch 1024 as the large-batch reference, the negative bank filled with random rather than selected negatives, and a variant where selection uses the online encoder instead of the momentum encoder.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Selected negatives should recover most of the kNN accuracy of the large-batch reference at batch 64, but the false negative rate should rise as selection becomes harder. We expect the random bank to perform no better than the standard queue.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does the augmentation graph spectrum tell us when more views stop helping
PROPOSAL: We examine the claim that contrastive learning performs spectral clustering on an augmentation graph by measuring, on real datasets, how the spectrum of the empirical augmentation kernel changes as augmentation strength increases, and whether the eigenvalue decay predicts the information that further views add. We estimate the augmentation graph on CIFAR-10 and STL-10 by sampling 64 views per image for a subset of 5000 images, embed them with a trained SimCLR ResNet-18, extract the top eigenvalues of the induced similarity matrix at four augmentation strengths, and correlate the eigengap with the marginal gain in linear probe accuracy obtained when the number of views per instance per epoch is doubled.
CONTROLS: Embeddings from a randomly initialised encoder and from a supervised encoder, a kernel built from pixel-space distances instead of embeddings, and shuffled pairings between eigengap and accuracy gain to calibrate the correlation.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: A larger eigengap should coincide with a smaller marginal gain from extra views, giving a usable criterion for when more views stop helping. The correlation may vanish if the subset is too small to estimate the spectrum reliably.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diffusion-generated views under a per-instance semantic distance target for small-batch SimCLR
PROPOSAL: We expand the set of views per instance with samples from a class-agnostic image diffusion model conditioned on the anchor through an image-to-image process with noise strength chosen per instance. The noise strength is raised until the cosine similarity between anchor and generated view under a frozen pretrained encoder drops to a target level, so that every instance receives views of comparable semantic distance rather than comparable pixel distortion. We train SimCLR with a ResNet-50 on ImageNet-100 at batch sizes 64 and 256, mixing one generated view with one standard view per instance, and evaluate linear probe and kNN accuracy, alignment and uniformity, and transfer to CIFAR-100.
CONTROLS: Standard augmentations alone at both batch sizes and at batch 2048, generated views at a fixed noise strength for all instances, generated views from an unconditioned diffusion sample matched to the anchor only by class, and views produced by strong hand-crafted augmentation tuned to the same average similarity, three seeds each.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: Per-instance noise strength should outperform fixed strength and should narrow the gap between batch 64 and batch 2048 by about half. Class-matched unconditioned samples should hurt alignment, confirming that the gain needs instance-level conditioning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: View scheduling from running per-instance information estimates
PROPOSAL: We allocate the number of augmented views drawn per instance in each epoch according to a running estimate of how much its recent views disagreed in embedding space, giving more views to instances whose views still carry fresh information and fewer to instances whose views have converged. The estimate is the exponential moving average of the per-instance InfoNCE loss computed under a momentum encoder. We train BYOL and SimCLR with ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet with a fixed total number of views per epoch equal to the standard two views per instance, so that the scheduler redistributes work rather than adding it, at batch sizes 64 and 256.
CONTROLS: Uniform two views per instance, allocation by a random score with the same histogram, allocation by the inverse of the score to check the direction of the effect, and allocation by class-level rather than instance-level averages.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Instance-level scheduling should improve linear probe accuracy by about one point on Tiny-ImageNet at batch 64 and less at batch 256. If the inverse allocation performs equally, the loss signal does not track view informativeness.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Information-Guided Latent View Expansion for Small-Batch SimCLR
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100 with a SimCLR objective at batch 128, adding a module that creates extra latent views of each instance by shifting its embedding along directions that raise an estimated information gain, computed as the drop in an InfoNCE bound when the new view joins the pair. A consistency term keeps each created view within a cosine radius of its anchor so that class content survives. Report linear probe accuracy, k-nearest-neighbour accuracy and transfer to CIFAR-10 and Flowers-102 after 400 epochs with a cosine learning rate schedule.
CONTROLS: Compare the module against plain SimCLR at batch 128 and against plain SimCLR at batch 1024 under the same schedule. Compare the module with and without the information gain guidance, using random directions instead. Compare the module against a stronger hand-crafted augmentation pipeline with the same number of views per instance. Repeat every setting over three seeds.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: The module should lift linear probe accuracy by one to two points over plain SimCLR at batch 128 and recover about half of the gain from the larger batch. The claim fails if the gain stays within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned Gated Generator of Extra Latent Views for Contrastive Pretraining
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a ResNet-18 with a SimCLR objective on CIFAR-100, attaching a lightweight module that maps each embedding to two further latent views through a gated residual layer trained with the contrastive loss itself. A temperature annealing rule raises the strength of the generated views over the first half of training, and a stop-gradient on the anchor stabilises optimisation. Evaluate with linear probe accuracy and k-nearest-neighbour accuracy on CIFAR-100, plus detection transfer on VOC, after 400 epochs with a step learning rate schedule at batch 128.
CONTROLS: Compare the module against plain SimCLR at batch 128 and against a supervised ResNet-18 under the same schedule. Compare the module with and without the projection head, using a random head instead. Compare the module against a deeper ResNet-50 backbone with the same number of views per instance. Repeat every setting over three seeds.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: The module should lift linear probe accuracy by one to two points over plain SimCLR at batch 128 and recover about half of the gain from the supervised network. The claim fails if the gain stays within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: How Much New Information Does an Extra View Bring? Gain-Ranked Views at Small Batch
PROPOSAL: Estimate, for every training instance, the mutual information a candidate view adds to the views already seen, using a variational InfoNCE estimate with a small critic network, and keep only the candidates with the largest estimated gain. Train a ResNet-18 with SimCLR on CIFAR-100 at batch 64 to 512, drawing candidates by interpolating between a view and its nearest neighbours in embedding space. Check that the instances with the highest estimated gain are also those whose k-nearest-neighbour error drops most after training, and report linear probe accuracy after 300 epochs.
CONTROLS: Vary the number of generated views per instance from one to eight while the batch is held fixed. Compare guided selection with a matched run that draws the same number of views from random candidates. Vary the batch while the number of generated views is held fixed. Repeat each configuration over three seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Gain-ranked selection should add about two points of probe accuracy at batch 64 and fade as the batch grows. The idea fails if random candidates reach the same accuracy at every batch, in which case the gain estimate carries little signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gain Estimates for Extra Views Under Changed Optimiser Choices at Small Batch
PROPOSAL: Estimate, for every training instance, the information a candidate view adds to the views already seen, using a variational InfoNCE estimate with a small critic network, and keep the candidates with the largest estimated gain. Train a ResNet-18 with SimCLR on CIFAR-100 at batch 128, drawing candidates by interpolating between a view and its nearest neighbours in embedding space. Report linear probe accuracy after 300 epochs, and describe how weight decay, optimiser type and crop scale interact with the selection rule across a family of training recipes.
CONTROLS: Vary the weight decay from small to large while the batch is held fixed. Compare guided selection with a matched run that draws the same number of views from random candidates at a different temperature. Vary the crop scale while the number of generated views is held fixed. Repeat each configuration over three seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Gain-ranked selection should add about two points of probe accuracy and remain stable across the recipes. The idea fails if its accuracy changes by more than a point from one recipe to the next, in which case the estimate carries little signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expanding View Diversity at Small Scale: Embedding-Space Mixing With a Semantic Guard
PROPOSAL: Create new views of each instance by mixing its embedding with embeddings of its augmented siblings under learned convex weights, then pass the mixed vector through a guard classifier trained on pseudo-labels from clustering so that only views keeping the same cluster are used as positives. Pretrain a ResNet-50 with SimCLR on ImageNet-100 at batch 128 for 200 epochs, and assess linear probe accuracy, cluster purity of the generated views, and transfer to Pets and Food-101 with fixed fine-tuning recipes.
CONTROLS: Compare the guarded method against plain SimCLR at batch 128 and against plain SimCLR at batch 512 under the same schedule. Repeat the comparison at batch 64 where memory limits bind. Compare the guard with a matched run that keeps every mixed view as a positive. Repeat every setting over three seeds.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The guarded method should match the accuracy of plain SimCLR at batch 512 while using a quarter of the batch. The claim fails if its accuracy at batch 64 is not above plain SimCLR at that batch, since the small regime is where it matters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prototype-Consistent Gaussian Views for Large-Batch Contrastive Pretraining
PROPOSAL: Generate new views of each instance by sampling from a Gaussian fitted to the embeddings of its augmented siblings, and keep a sample only when its nearest centre among a bank of online cluster prototypes is unchanged. Pretrain a ResNet-50 with SimCLR on ImageNet-100 at batch 4096 for 200 epochs. Report linear probe accuracy, the rate of prototype agreement for generated samples, and transfer to Pets and Food-101 with fixed probe recipes.
CONTROLS: Compare the guarded method against plain SimCLR at batch 4096 and against plain SimCLR at batch 8192 under the same schedule. Repeat the comparison at batch 2048 where memory limits bind. Compare the guard with a matched run that keeps every sampled view as a positive. Repeat every setting over three seeds.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The guarded method should match the accuracy of plain SimCLR at batch 8192 while using half of the batch. The claim fails if its accuracy at batch 2048 is not above plain SimCLR at that batch, since that regime is where it matters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Instance-Wise Information Gain of Augmented Views Tracked Through Contrastive Training
PROPOSAL: Track, for a ResNet-18 trained with SimCLR on STL-10 and CIFAR-100, how much each additional augmented view of an instance reduces the conditional entropy of its embedding given the views already seen, estimated with a nearest-neighbour entropy estimator on held-out instances every ten epochs. Build a view scheduler that stops adding views to an instance once its measured gain falls below a threshold, and spend the saved computation on more instances per update. Report linear probe accuracy at batch 128 after 500 epochs and the relation between the gain curve and downstream error.
CONTROLS: Measure linear probe accuracy and class-wise error for the scheduler and for fixed view counts. Compare the measured gain with downstream error on the same held-out instances. Compare the scheduler against a matched run that stops views at random with the same average count. Repeat each measurement over three seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Instances whose gain falls early should show lower downstream error, and the scheduler should keep probe accuracy while cutting views by a third. The idea fails if the gain curve is uncorrelated with downstream error.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training Dynamics of Alignment and Uniformity Under Adaptive View Plans
PROPOSAL: Follow, for a ResNet-18 trained with SimCLR on STL-10 and CIFAR-100, how the alignment and uniformity statistics of the embedding evolve while a view scheduler adds augmented views to each instance until the contrastive objective reaches a target value, measured every ten epochs on training instances. Spend the saved computation on more instances per update, and report the smoothness of the optimisation trajectory, the final objective value, and wall-clock efficiency at batch 128 after 500 epochs.
CONTROLS: Measure alignment and uniformity statistics for the scheduler and for fixed view counts. Compare the measured objective value with smoothness on the same training instances. Compare the scheduler against a matched run that stops views at random with the same average count. Repeat each measurement over three seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The scheduler should reach lower alignment values earlier and keep uniformity statistics steady while cutting views by a third. The idea fails if the objective value is uncorrelated with the smoothness of the trajectory.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Same-Compute Comparison of Learned View Expansion and Large-Batch SimCLR
PROPOSAL: Implement a view expander that adds one perturbed latent view per instance, shifted along the leading directions of the local covariance of its neighbours, and train a ResNet-18 with SimCLR on CIFAR-10 at batch 128 for 200 epochs. Give the large-batch alternative the same count of forward passes per update by raising the batch to 256. Report linear probe accuracy, k-nearest-neighbour accuracy and the number of positive pairs per update, using the learning rate schedule of the original SimCLR recipe.
CONTROLS: Compare the expander against plain SimCLR at batch 256 with the same number of forward passes per update. Compare the expander against a hand-crafted extra augmentation with the same number of views per instance. Compare the expander with and without the neighbour covariance, using isotropic noise instead. Repeat every setting over three seeds.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The expander should reach probe accuracy within half a point of batch 256 while holding the batch at 128. The claim fails if the larger batch with the same passes per update is clearly better.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent View Expansion Against Shorter Runs and Smaller Training Sets
PROPOSAL: Build a view expander that appends a single perturbed latent view for every instance, displaced along the main axes of the covariance among its neighbours, and train a ResNet-18 using SimCLR on CIFAR-10 at batch 128 across 200 epochs. Run the alternative recipes with a lower training length and with half of the training set. Report linear probe accuracy, k-nearest-neighbour accuracy and the count of positive pairs per update, following the original SimCLR learning rate schedule.
CONTROLS: Compare the expander against plain SimCLR at batch 128 with half the number of epochs. Compare the expander against a hand-crafted extra augmentation with half the number of images per class. Compare the expander with and without the neighbour covariance, using isotropic noise instead. Repeat every setting over three seeds.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The expander should reach probe accuracy within half a point of the full-length run while holding the batch at 128. The claim fails if the shorter run is clearly better.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Characterising view information gain as a conditional entropy and validating it by ablation
PROPOSAL: We define the information a view adds for an instance as the entropy of the view embedding conditional on the anchor embedding under a momentum encoder, estimate it per instance with a variational decoder, and test whether the quantity has predictive content: we rank instances by the estimate, remove augmentation for the top and bottom deciles in separate SimCLR ResNet-18 runs on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100, and measure the resulting change in linear probe accuracy.
CONTROLS: Random deciles of the same size, ranking by loss value, the estimate recomputed on a frozen encoder, and three seeds.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The top decile removal should cost at least four times as much accuracy as the bottom decile removal. The definition is refuted if the ranking is no better than loss value or than random.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mapping the training dynamics of contrastive learning through loss curvature
PROPOSAL: We characterise the information landscape of contrastive training by tracking, across training, the leading eigenvalues of the loss Hessian and the effective rank of the representation for SimCLR ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100 at two batch sizes, using power iteration on mini-batches every few epochs. We then relate the moment at which the effective rank plateaus to the final linear probe accuracy across learning rate and temperature settings, producing a description of how the geometry of the loss evolves from early to late training.
CONTROLS: Supervised training with the same backbone as a reference trajectory, a randomly initialised encoder for the starting point, and three seeds.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Effective rank should plateau earlier at the larger batch, and the plateau epoch should predict final accuracy within two points. The result is refuted if the plateau epoch varies more across seeds than across settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive view generation with a learned generator constrained by neighbour agreement
PROPOSAL: We train a conditional generator that produces new views of each image in pixel space from the anchor and a noise code, with the contrastive encoder and generator updated alternately: the generator is rewarded for producing views whose embeddings are far from the anchor's existing views while a kNN agreement term, computed under a frozen copy of the encoder, keeps the generated view inside the anchor's neighbourhood. The amount of expansion per instance follows the gap between those two terms, so instances with converged views receive more diverse generations. SimCLR with ResNet-50 runs on ImageNet-100 and STL-10 at batch 64 and 256.
CONTROLS: Standard augmentations at both batch sizes and at batch 2048, the generator without the agreement term, a fixed-strength generator, and three seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The adaptive generator should recover most of the gap to batch 2048 on STL-10 and about half on ImageNet-100. It fails if the generator without the agreement term performs as well, which would mean semantic control is not needed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Recovering large-batch negatives on small hardware by cached gradient accumulation
PROPOSAL: We reproduce the effect of a large batch on hardware that holds only a small one by computing embeddings for several micro-batches without gradients, caching them, then recomputing each micro-batch with gradients against the full cached set of negatives, so that the contrastive loss sees an effective batch of 2048 while memory holds 64 images. SimCLR with ResNet-50 runs on ImageNet-100 and STL-10, and we compare against true large-batch training on linear probe and kNN accuracy and on wall-clock throughput.
CONTROLS: True large-batch training as the reference, plain batch 64 as the floor, MoCo v2 with a queue of the same size as the cache, the cache refreshed at two frequencies within a step, and three seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Cached accumulation should match true batch 2048 within half a point at about twice the wall-clock time of plain batch 64. It is refuted if staleness of cached embeddings within a step degrades accuracy by more than one point.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-instance temperature from view agreement for small-batch contrastive training
PROPOSAL: We manage the invariance-expressivity trade-off per instance by setting each anchor's InfoNCE temperature from the cosine agreement of its views under a momentum encoder, sharpening anchors whose views already agree and relaxing anchors whose views differ, and we test it where the question bites: SimCLR and MoCo v2 with ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet at batch 32 and 64.
CONTROLS: Fixed temperature tuned per batch size, a decaying global temperature, temperature from a shuffled agreement vector, a large batch as reference, three seeds.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Adaptive temperature should recover a third of the gap between the small and the large batch on Tiny-ImageNet. It is refuted if the shuffled assignment performs the same.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A sweep of temperature and augmentation strength at batch 2048
PROPOSAL: We map the trade-off between invariance and expressivity by running SimCLR with ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet at batch 2048 over a grid of five fixed temperatures and four augmentation strengths, measuring linear probe accuracy on class labels, probe accuracy on augmentation parameters as an expressivity readout, and alignment and uniformity, then fitting a response surface that locates the best temperature for each strength.
CONTROLS: A supervised ResNet-18 as reference, a randomly initialised encoder as floor, a placebo probe on shuffled labels to mark chance level, the probe retrained with two schedule lengths, three seeds.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The best temperature should fall as augmentation strength rises, with the surface explaining most of the variance in probe accuracy. It is refuted if the grid optimum differs across seeds by more than one cell.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling adaptive view expansion to full ImageNet at small batch
PROPOSAL: We take the strongest adaptive view scheme from a pilot, latent extrapolation along queue-neighbour directions with a per-instance step chosen so that kNN agreement under a frozen encoder stays above a threshold, and test whether its gains hold at scale: MoCo v2 with ResNet-50 on full ImageNet at batch 128 and 256, with the step distribution logged per class so that we can see which instances receive the most expansion. We evaluate linear probe accuracy, kNN accuracy, alignment and uniformity, and transfer to ten classification datasets.
CONTROLS: MoCo v2 at the same batches without expansion, MoCo v2 at batch 4096 as the ceiling, random directions as placebo, the threshold set at two levels, loss curves inspected for collapse, and two seeds given the scale.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Expansion should recover more than half of the gap to batch 4096 on linear probe accuracy and nearly all on transfer. It fails if random directions recover as much, which would place the gain in regularisation rather than in neighbourhood structure.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling a large self-supervised teacher into a small-batch student
PROPOSAL: We train a ResNet-50 student on full ImageNet at batch 128 to match the embeddings of a frozen vision transformer teacher pretrained by self-distillation, using a cosine loss on the two standard views of each image plus the contrastive loss of MoCo v2, so that the student benefits from the teacher's view invariances without large batches. We evaluate linear probe accuracy, kNN accuracy and transfer to ten classification datasets, and we report how much of the teacher's accuracy the student retains at each batch size.
CONTROLS: MoCo v2 alone at batch 128, the distillation loss alone, the teacher's own linear probe as the ceiling, a run at batch 256 to see whether the gap to the teacher narrows with batch size, and two seeds.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The student should land within two points of the teacher on linear probe accuracy at batch 128. It fails if distillation alone matches the combined loss, meaning the contrastive term adds nothing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Interpolated augmentation chains as controlled view expansion on CIFAR
PROPOSAL: We expand view diversity in a controlled way by composing the standard SimCLR augmentations into a chain of intermediate views whose semantic distance from the anchor grows in fixed steps, and we weight each intermediate view in the loss by a per-instance factor that falls when a frozen encoder's kNN agreement with the anchor drops. ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 at batch 32 and 128, with the chain length chosen on a validation split.
CONTROLS: Two views only, the chain with uniform weights, weights from a shuffled agreement vector, batch 1024 as reference, three seeds.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Weighted chains should beat two views by about one point at batch 32 and by nothing at batch 1024. It fails if uniform weights do as well.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Trading batch size for training length in contrastive learning on CIFAR
PROPOSAL: We test whether the deficit of small batches is a matter of optimisation steps by training SimCLR with ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 at batch 32 and 128 for up to eight times the standard number of epochs, with the learning rate rescaled by the square root of the batch ratio, and we record linear probe and kNN accuracy at each doubling of training length, producing a curve of accuracy against total optimisation steps for each batch size.
CONTROLS: Batch 1024 for the standard length as reference, a constant learning rate without rescaling, and three seeds.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Small-batch runs should approach the batch 1024 accuracy as steps grow, with the residual gap under one point at eight times the length. It fails if the gap stops shrinking after the second doubling.
